pages.title: Room Air Monitor
pages.text: An always-visible wall screen. Place it inside a sealed room; no menu is needed. Supply and demand use breathing-rate units: one Survival or Adventure player draws 1 unit. Creative and spectator players draw none.$(br2)This first release measures load. Overload does not yet shut down burners or deplete room oxygen.

pages.title: Shared Supply
pages.text: SUPPLY and DEMAND describe the whole shared pool. LOCAL is this room’s demand. A Core touching two rooms shares one 8-unit output; it does not produce 8 for each room. Overlapping sources add once.$(br2)Sources must be inside or directly touch the room. Range alone cannot deliver air through unrelated walls.

pages.title: Reading the Screen
pages.text: Green: supported. Flashing yellow: at least 80% capacity, overloaded, or trapped air without production. Red: no air or no seal in vacuum. Gray WAITING: geometry or consumer indexing is incomplete.$(br2)These are status and rate readings, not an O2 percentage. Room tanks and reserve-time readings are planned.

pages.title: Consumers
pages.text: Torch or lantern: 0.25. Each lit candle: 0.25. Fire or campfire: 1. Furnace, smoker or blast furnace: 3. Animals add demand.$(br2)Soul flames, Thermal Heaters, Returned and Architects draw none. Airlock reserves remain dedicated to cycling.$(br2)Comparator: 8 for strain/near capacity, 15 for no air/seal, 4 for no supply, otherwise 0.
Four iron, two copper, two redstone and one glass. The panel observes air; it does not manufacture it. ORSA advises against arguing with the numbers.

pages.title: Warning Cues
pages.text: A short chime warns when a nearby gauge enters STRAINED. The klaxon sounds only when you are approaching suffocation, after suit and tank protection are checked, even without a gauge. NO SEAL and NO AIR remain red visual warnings. Several nearby panels produce one warning per listener. Critical warnings repeat at most every ten seconds; there is no speech.$(br2)Near-capacity yellow alone is quiet. This first accounting build reports overload; automatic combustion starvation and overload suffocation follow in the next stage.
